theme: 호기심 어린 불신 — 가장 효과적인 신제품 광고

overview.theme_ko: 호기심 어린 불신과 신제품 광고 효과
overview.topic: 🔎 과장 광고에 대한 불신을 호기심이 압도해 제품 시도로 이어지는 현상
overview.stance_reason: Maloney의 연구 결과를 근거로 사실을 설명·제시하며 주관적 찬반을 드러내지 않음
overview.structure_reason: Maloney의 제안(주장) → 주부 표본 대상 study와 18%·44%·34% 결과(근거) → 결론

key_grammar.source_sentence: In a consumer research classic, Maloney proposed that the disbelief most people experience when encountering exaggerated product claims is often overwhelmed by a natural curiosity.

explanation.text: 'the disbelief most people experience'는 the disbelief 뒤에 목적격 관계대명사 that/which가 생략된 형태로, most people experience가 앞의 disbelief를 꾸며 준다(목적격 관계대명사 생략).
관계대명사가 관계절 안에서 목적어 역할을 하면 생략할 수 있다(주격은 원칙적으로 생략 불가).
명사 바로 뒤에 '주어+동사'가 이어지고 그 동사의 목적어 자리가 비어 있으면 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 것이다(experience의 목적어가 없음).
수식어구 most people experience ... claims를 걷어내면 문장의 진짜 주어는 단수 the disbelief이므로 동사는 is로 수일치한다.
주격 관계대명사가 쓰인 who clearly disbelieved the message(7번 문장)와 달리, 여기서는 목적격이라 생략이 가능하다.

key_grammar.example_analysis: the disbelief와 most people experience 사이에 목적격 관계대명사 that(which)이 생략되어 있다.

drills.question: 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?
drills.sentence: In a consumer research classic, Maloney proposed [[1|that]] the disbelief most people [[2|experience]] when [[3|encountering]] exaggerated product claims [[4|are]] often [[5|overwhelmed]] by a natural curiosity.
drills.fix: 문장의 진짜 주어는 단수명사 the disbelief이고 most people experience ... claims는 이를 꾸미는 수식어이므로, are가 아니라 원문대로 is가 맞다.

drills.question: 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 것을 고르시오.
drills.sentence: This is often [[done/doing]] by yielding to the message and [[trying/tried]] out the product in an attempt [[to readjust/readjusting]] personal attitudes toward the brand.
drills.fix: is 뒤이므로 수동태 done, 전치사 by의 목적어로 yielding과 병렬을 이루는 동명사 trying, an attempt를 수식하는 to부정사 to readjust가 옳다.

drills.question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
drills.answer: Convincing consumers that the claims about a new product are true are not necessary to create interest in product trial.
drills.fix: 문장의 주어는 동명사구 Convincing consumers ...(단수 취급)이므로 술어동사는 are가 아니라 원문대로 is가 맞다.
options: ① When advertising information conflicts with existing beliefs, the resulting disagreement must be somehow resolved.
② The latter was tied into beliefs that actual product experience was necessary to fully judge the claims.
③ Convincing consumers that the claims about a new product are true are not necessary to create interest in product trial.
④ Few consumers who clearly disbelieved the message were interested in trying the product (18%).
⑤ The results suggest that advertising that causes consumers not to believe the message claims but makes them curious may be the most effective form of new product advertising.

drills.question: 소비자들이 접하는 그 광고는 종종 과장된 주장을 담고 있다. (관계대명사를 쓰지 말고 배열)
drills.answer: The advertisement consumers encounter often contains exaggerated claims.

drills.question: 한 소비자 연구의 고전에서, Maloney는 대부분의 사람들이 과장된 제품 주장을 접할 때 경험하는 불신이 종종 자연스러운 호기심에 압도된다고 제안했다.
drills.answer: In a consumer research classic, Maloney proposed that the disbelief most people experience when encountering exaggerated product claims is often overwhelmed by a natural curiosity.

flow_blocks.easy_example: 궁금증이 있는 쪽이 오히려 가장 많이 사 보려 함.

flow_blocks.summary: 믿게 하기보다 [[호기심]]을 유발하는 광고가 신제품에 가장 효과적

sentences.english: In a consumer research classic, Maloney proposed that the disbelief most people experience when encountering exaggerated product claims is often overwhelmed by a natural curiosity.

grammar.note: the disbelief 뒤 목적격 관계대명사 that/which 생략, most people experience가 수식
when + 현재분사, 주어(they) 생략된 시간 부사절

chunks.en: In a consumer research classic,
Maloney proposed that the disbelief most people experience
when encountering exaggerated product claims
is often overwhelmed by a natural curiosity.

misreads.statement: Maloney에 따르면, 사람들이 과장된 제품 주장에 대해 느끼는 불신이 대개 자연스러운 호기심을 억눌러 버린다.
misreads.anchor: is often overwhelmed by a natural curiosity
misreads.why: 불신이 호기심을 억누르는 것이 아니라 호기심에 '압도되는' 것으로, 주체·대상이 뒤바뀜

misreads.statement: 'most people experience'는 a natural curiosity를 수식하여, 사람들이 자연스러운 호기심을 경험한다는 뜻이다.
misreads.why: most people experience는 curiosity가 아니라 앞의 disbelief(불신)를 꾸미는 관계절이다

mistips: the disbelief 뒤에 목적격 관계대명사 that/which가 생략됨 → most people experience가 disbelief를 수식하고, 문장의 진짜 주어는 단수 the disbelief라 동사는 is.

sentences.english: When advertising information conflicts with existing beliefs, the resulting disagreement must be somehow resolved.

grammar.note: must be + p.p., '해소되어야 한다'는 조동사 수동

chunks.en: When advertising information conflicts with existing beliefs,
the resulting disagreement must be somehow resolved.
chunks.ko: 그 결과로 생긴 [[불일치]]는 어떻게든 해소되어야 한다.

misreads.statement: 광고 정보가 기존 신념과 충돌하면, 그로 인해 생긴 불일치는 어떻게든 해소되어야 한다.

sentences.english: This is often done by yielding to the message and trying out the product in an attempt to readjust personal attitudes toward the brand.

chunks.en: This is often done
by yielding to the message
and trying out the product
in an attempt to readjust personal attitudes toward the brand.

misreads.statement: 이 불일치 해소는 대개 메시지를 거부하고 제품 구매를 미룸으로써 이루어진다.
misreads.anchor: yielding to the message and trying out the product
misreads.why: 메시지를 거부하는 게 아니라 메시지에 굴복(수용)하고 제품을 시도함으로써 해소한다

sentences.english: In his study, a sample of housewives was exposed to advertisements for food products and then divided into two groups: those participants that found the ad claims to be believable and the others that thought they were hard to believe.

chunks.en: In his study, a sample of housewives
was exposed to advertisements for food products
and then divided into two groups:
those participants that found the ad claims to be believable
and the others that thought they were hard to believe.

misreads.statement: 'thought they were hard to believe'에서 they는 광고를 본 주부들을 가리킨다.
misreads.anchor: the others that thought they were hard to believe
misreads.why: they는 주부가 아니라 앞의 the ad claims(광고 주장)를 가리킨다

sentences.english: The latter group was further divided into two groups, those who confidently disbelieved the claims and those who had what Maloney described as a curious nonbelief.

grammar.note: 선행사를 포함해 '~하는 것'을 뜻하는 명사절, had의 목적어

chunks.en: The latter group was further divided into two groups,
those who confidently disbelieved the claims
and those who had
what Maloney described as a curious nonbelief.

misreads.statement: 여기서 'The latter group'은 광고 주장을 믿을 만하다고 여긴 참가자들을 가리킨다.
misreads.anchor: the others that thought they were hard to believe
misreads.why: the latter group은 믿은 집단이 아니라 믿기 어렵다고 여긴 집단을 가리킨다

mistips: what Maloney described as a curious nonbelief는 선행사 없이 what이 이끄는 명사절로, 앞 동사 had의 목적어다.

sentences.english: The latter was tied into beliefs that actual product experience was necessary to fully judge the claims.

chunks.en: The latter was tied into beliefs
that actual product experience was necessary
to fully judge the claims.

misreads.statement: 이 지문은 주부들이 실제로 어떤 식품 브랜드를 더 선호했는지 구체적 상표명까지 밝히고 있다.
misreads.anchor: actual product experience was necessary to fully judge the claims
misreads.why: 본문은 실제 제품 경험이 필요하다는 믿음만 언급하며 구체적 선호 상표는 다루지 않는다

sentences.english: Few consumers who clearly disbelieved the message were interested in trying the product (18%).

chunks.en: Few consumers who clearly disbelieved the message
were interested in trying the product (18%).

misreads.statement: 메시지를 분명히 불신한 소비자 중 제품을 시도하려는 사람은 극소수(18%)였다.
확고히 불신한 소비자 다수가 결국 제품을 시도했다.
misreads.anchor: Few consumers who clearly disbelieved the message were interested in trying the product
misreads.english: Most consumers who firmly disbelieved the message ended up trying the product.

sentences.english: However, Maloney's results showed that more consumers who were in the curious nonbelief group were ready to try the product (44%) than in the group that expressed no concerns about (i.e., believed) the advertising claims (34%).

chunks.en: However, Maloney's results showed that
more consumers who were in the curious nonbelief group
chunks.ko: [[호기심 어린 불신 집단]]에 있던 더 많은 [[소비자]]가

chunks.en: were ready to try the product (44%)
than in the group that expressed no concerns about
(i.e., believed) the advertising claims (34%).

misreads.statement: 호기심 어린 불신 집단(44%)이 광고를 믿은 집단(34%)보다 제품을 시도할 의향이 더 높았다.

mistips: 'more consumers ~ (44%) than in the group ~ (34%)'는 more ~ than 비교 구문으로, 44% 집단과 34% 집단을 비교하고 있다.

sentences.english: The results suggest that advertising that causes consumers not to believe the message claims but makes them curious may be the most effective form of new product advertising.

grammar.note: cause 목적어를 '~하지 않게 하다', not이 부정사 부정
causes ~ but makes로 두 동사가 병렬

chunks.en: The results suggest that advertising
that causes consumers not to believe the message claims
but makes them curious
may be the most effective form of new product advertising.

misreads.statement: 필자는 소비자가 광고를 믿지 않게 만드는 광고가 가장 효과적이라고 보는데, 그 이유는 불신 자체가 제품 구매를 강제하기 때문이다.
misreads.anchor: but makes them curious may be the most effective form of new product advertising
misreads.why: 효과적인 이유는 불신 자체가 아니라 호기심을 유발하기 때문이다

mistips: that causes ~ not to believe ~ but makes them curious에서 causes와 makes가 병렬로, 둘 다 advertising을 선행사로 하는 관계절 동사다.

sentences.english: Convincing consumers that the claims about a new product are true is not necessary to create interest in product trial.

chunks.en: Convincing consumers that the claims about a new product are true
is not necessary to create interest in product trial.
chunks.ko: 제품 시도에 대한 [[관심]]을 만드는 데 필요하지 않다.

misreads.statement: 필자는 신제품 시도 관심을 이끌어내려면 소비자에게 광고 주장이 사실임을 반드시 납득시켜야 한다고 본다.
misreads.anchor: is not necessary to create interest in product trial
misreads.why: 주장이 사실임을 납득시키는 것은 필요하지 않다고 필자는 말한다
